correctness.rationale: Writing N(z)=b+dz and N(v)=Av+ℓ(v)z, the horizontal component of torsion on (v,z) forces ω(v,b)b=0 for every v, hence b=0. The remaining torsion is precisely ω((A−dI)v,(A−dI)w)z, with no condition on ℓ. This is bidirectional and uses neither division by 2 nor algebraic closedness. For rank(S)=r, successively choosing an independent orthogonal frame gives ∏(q^(2m−i)−q^i); dividing by the number of bases and multiplying by the number of surjections V→W and q^(2m+1) gives the claimed count. Independent small-matrix enumerations reproduced (1,9), (1,32), (1,225,3150) for (m,q)=(1,2),(1,3),(2,2), before the scalar and functional factors. The isotropic Grassmannian has codimension binom(r,2): the tangent map to the alternating restriction is surjective even in characteristic two, by choosing a triangular representative bilinear form and lifting it through V/W→W*. Isotropic frames form iterated open vector bundles, which gives geometric irreducibility of the Grassmannian. Surjections onto the tautological r-plane form an open vector-bundle locus, giving the stated rank-stratum dimension. Every isotropic image extends to a Lagrangian; the Lagrangian incidence bundle maps onto the reduced variety and its rank-m part is dense, giving the full dimension. The rank statistic is rank(S), not rank(N); no claim about nonreduced torsion schemes is verified.
